comment: Nuphos -> Cerin rename map. Rules run in order on every tracked text file except exclude_paths. Each rule must be idempotent: its output never matches its own pattern.

rules.name: product-name
rules.why: The product name, wherever a person can read it (UI, copy, docs, comments).

rules.name: url-scheme
rules.why: Deep links the apps hand out. Inbound handlers keep nuphos:// as a hidden legacy alias (see keep.txt).

rules.name: hosts
rules.why: nuphos.ai and api.nuphos.ai -> platform.cerin.ai (desktop already uses it for both API and web); other subdomains keep their prefix, including in user@host and mailto test fixtures. telemetry.nuphos.ai is upstream's own endpoint and stays (keep.txt).

rules.name: lookalike-host
rules.why: Tests that reject a lookalike of the real host.

rules.name: hosts-upper
rules.why: Case-folding tests.

rules.name: client-id-interpolated
rules.why: Versioned app client ids. Static legacy ids stay accepted by every parser.

rules.name: client-id-rust-cli
rules.why: The two Rust compile-time client ids.

rules.name: client-id-ios-analytics
rules.why: The iOS analytics client property.

rules.name: client-id-ios-analytics-doc
rules.why: The documented iOS analytics client property.

rules.name: discord-slash-command
rules.why: Visible Discord help prefers the primary command; the registered legacy command still parses.

rules.name: slack-slash-command
rules.why: Visible Slack help prefers the primary command; the registered legacy command still parses.

rules.name: admin-command
rules.why: The image installs both admin command names; visible instructions prefer Cerin.

rules.name: box-agent-inline-code
rules.why: Inline-code references to the Box CLI use the primary name, including escaped TypeScript templates.

rules.name: cli-device-login
rules.why: The installer provides both CLI names; visible instructions prefer Cerin.

rules.name: cli-agent-join
rules.why: The installer provides both CLI names; visible join instructions prefer Cerin.

rules.name: runtime-error-prefix
rules.why: Runtime diagnostics use the product's current name.

rules.name: regex-url-scheme
rules.why: Regex fixtures for outbound links use the primary scheme.

rules.name: current-repository
rules.why: Links, workflow guards and release feeds for this repository use its current owner and name. Generic GitHub fixtures and Android's external WIF policy stay unchanged.

rules.name: repository-clone-directory
rules.why: The runtime build instructions enter the directory created by cloning this repository.

rules.name: android-official-repository-doc
rules.why: Android release administration happens in this repository; the separate WIF subject remains a legacy external policy.

rules.name: repository-action-target
rules.why: The GitHub App token action targets this repository by its repository-only name.

rules.name: renovate-app-example
rules.why: The example name for a newly created Renovate GitHub App uses Cerin.

rules.name: current-repository-owner-doc
rules.why: The contributor setup names this repository's current owner.

rules.name: apple-release-team
rules.why: Desktop and CLI releases use The New Binary's Apple team; installed iOS signing metadata is unchanged.

rules.name: mongo-example-database
rules.why: The editable example database name uses the current product name; existing database names are unchanged.

rules.name: team-export-filename
rules.why: The team export download uses the current product name.

rules.name: example-host
rules.why: Test fixtures.
